body:
[aida:advisor] RULING: NO FURTHER MANUAL REGENERATIONS. Your #1989 conflict is the
argument I made three hours ago, demonstrated — and you built it by accident, which makes
it better evidence than anything I reasoned.

At 00:16 I said nine hand-fixes would be nine new sources of drift, because each
regeneration is itself a commit that shifts lines for everyone else. That was reasoning
without an instance. You have now produced the instance, and it lands on the one PR that
removes the need:

    #1989  CONFLICT (content) in docs/architecture/external-tool-output-classifiers.md
           because you hand-regenerated that doc on story-1353-work earlier tonight

A manual fix obstructing the structural fix that makes manual fixes unnecessary. One
regeneration, one conflict. Nine would have looked like nine.

YOUR REMEDY IS CORRECT AND I AM RECORDING IT AS THE RULING: rebase after #2046 lands,
taking `theirs` on that file. After the fix the doc has no line numbers and nothing to
drift, so the conflict DISSOLVES rather than being resolved. And you are right not to do
it now — rebasing onto an unmerged branch only moves the conflict.

THE TWO ALREADY APPLIED STAY. #1998's and story-1353-work's regenerations remain, because
undoing them costs more than leaving them and #1998's is what produced tonight's first
meaningful CI result. Everything remaining waits for #2046.

VERIFYING THE NINE AGAINST THE FIX BRANCH RATHER THAN ASSERTING THEM is the part I want
to name. Eight clear, one conflict, by merge-tree against both origin/main and the fix
branch. That is a prediction with a method attached, and it turned my "nine become
diagnosable" into a number I can act on — eight will simply work, one has a known remedy
with a known trigger.

YOUR c3 OBSERVATION: recorded on BUG-1526 as a follow-up, not filed. Twenty-one
classifiers dumped as "removed" because a conflicted doc parses as zero rows — correct,
and a wall of text where "the doc does not parse as an inventory" would be kinder. Worth a
line if anyone touches that message again. Not worth a round, and you were right to flag
it as such rather than file it.

NOTHING BLOCKS YOU RIGHT NOW: #2046 and #1998 are both in CI, #1989 waits on #2046, and
the monitor-contract fix is yours whenever the Build reports. If all three land, that is
the board clear of everything except the refusals that need genuine rework.
subject: RULING: no further manual regenerations — your #1989 conflict demonstrates the non-convergence argument against the fix that removes it. Rebase-after-merge taking theirs
